characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: SmartLab SE X-ray diffractometer with Cu Kα radiation (λ = 0.154060 nm)
characterization_methods.key_findings: Both the initial and the -196 °C held samples show only γ(111), γ(200), γ(220) and γ(311) reflections with no extra peaks, confirming a fully austenitic microstructure and no isothermal martensite formation at -196 °C.
characterization_methods.purpose: To verify the absence of isothermal martensite in the initial as-forged steel and after holding at -196 °C for 30 min

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: Apreo S HiVac scanning electron microscope (SEM)
characterization_methods.key_findings: Fully indexed equiaxed grain structure; the phase map shows a single indexed phase (austenite) with no second-phase regions.
characterization_methods.purpose: To analyze the initial (as-forged) microstructure via IPF map and phase map

analytical_models.equation_role: Estimates the stacking fault energy of the austenitic steel at different temperatures
analytical_models.model_note: Using equations (2)-(4) and Table 1 parameters, the SFE of the experimental steel at -196 °C, -77 °C and RT is estimated to be 32, 40 and 61 mJ/m², respectively.

parameters.name: ΔG_Fe^(γ→ε) / ΔG_Mn / ΔG_Al / ΔG_C / ΔG_FeMn / ΔG_FeAl / ΔG_FeC / ΔG_FeMnAl/C

computational_details.simulation_method: Thermodynamic calculation of stacking fault energy (SFE) using the regular-solution free-energy formulation

processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: The experimental steel was melted and cast in a 50 kg vacuum induction furnace and then air cooled to RT.
The ingot was reheated to 1250 °C and held for 2 h for homogenization.
The ingot was forged into round bars with a diameter of 60 mm followed by cooling to RT in the furnace; starting and finishing forging temperatures were 1100 and 950 °C, respectively.

processing_steps.method: holding in liquid nitrogen followed by XRD analysis
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Another sample was held at liquid nitrogen (-196 °C) for 30 min followed by XRD analysis to verify the absence of isothermal martensite.

structures.overall_structure: Fully austenitic (single-phase fcc γ) equiaxed-grain microstructure; holding in liquid nitrogen at -196 °C for 30 min produced no isothermal martensite, indicating a very stable austenite.

unmapped_findings: The stacking fault energy (SFE) of the experimental steel is estimated to be 32 mJ/m² at -196 °C, compared with 40 mJ/m² at -77 °C and 61 mJ/m² at RT; a SFE of 32 mJ/m² at -196 °C still fully suppresses deformation-induced martensitic transformation (DIMT) but enables mechanical twinning.

Holding in liquid nitrogen at -196 °C for 30 min produces no isothermal martensite, indicating a very stable austenite; the initial as-forged microstructure consists of equiaxed grains with a fully austenitic constituent.
The alloy composition of this sample is Fe-20Mn-6Al-0.6C-0.15Si; its density estimated by the Kim et al. equation is 7.078 g/cm³ and the measured density is 7.114 g/cm³.

Note on scope: the tensile tests and Charpy impact tests at -196 °C were carried out on separate tensile-deformed and impact-tested samples, not on this sample that was only held in liquid nitrogen for 30 min and analysed by XRD; those mechanical/impact data therefore are not assigned to this sample.
